items.title: Australia Says Negotiations Continue on Gas Reservation Proposal
items.author: Amy Bainbridge
items.content: <article>The Australian government says negotiations over its gas reservation proposals are continuing and it hopes the legislation will pass parliament in the coming week.</article>

items.title: China’s Top Planner Seeks Faster Construction of State Projects
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China’s top planning agency urged local authorities to speed up the construction of government investment projects and disbursement of funds in a bid to spur growth in the world’s second-largest economy.</article>

items.title: China Military Bans SF Express From Procurement Over Misconduct
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>SF Express Co., a leading Chinese delivery and logistics company, has been suspended from participating in military-wide procurement of goods, engineering and services over alleged violations.</article>

items.title: Vietnam Amends Laws to Speed Land Clearance, Development of New Projects
items.author: Nguyen Dieu Tu Uyen
items.content: <article>Vietnam’s National Assembly passed land law amendments aimed at speeding up site clearance and unblocking of property and infrastructure projects as the government seeks to achieve its multiyear double-digit economic growth target.</article>

items.title: Peru Rattled by 6.7-Magnitude Quake, With No Casualties Reported
items.author: Carla Samon Ros
items.content: <article>Peru was shaken by a powerful earthquake late Friday that damaged some houses and disrupted power in a central district.</article>

items.title: J&J Snack Foods CEO on 4Q Results and Consumer Sentiment
items.content: <article>J&J Snack Foods CEO Dan Fachner said the company’s turnaround is on track after a strong year, citing Project Apollo’s more than $25 million in durable savings. A second phase, Apollo 2, is expected to generate another $5 million by 2027 through distribution and manufacturing improvements. Fachner speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Salvadoran Troops Killed in Haiti Blast Amid Rescue Mission
items.author: David Alire Garcia
items.content: <article>Three Salvadoran soldiers died in Haiti after an explosion struck an area where they were working, weeks after President Nayib Bukele ordered a large deployment to the Caribbean island nation to find missing troops.</article>

items.title: Trump Says Huang Should Return to Nvidia After ‘Big Apology’
items.content: <article>President Trump called for Jensen Huang to make a big apology and return as CEO of Nvidia even as the prospect remains highly unlikely.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: ‘Always Remain Liquid’: Richards
items.content: <article>Bruce Richards, managing partner and head of CVC Marathon, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on “Bloomberg Money.” They discuss Richards’ favorite investing advice he has received throughout his career. Richards warns about irrational markets and also says he’s not a fan of leveraged ETF structures. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: S&P, Dow Slide Into Correction as Investors Dump Tech
items.content: <article>Chipmakers led a plunge in US stocks on Friday, with the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Index closing in correction territory. Carmen Reinicke reports. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Adjusting for Credit Risk: Masters In Business with David Eichhorn
items.content: <article>Barry speaks with David Eichhorn, CEO and Head of Investment Strategies at NISA Investment Advisors. They discuss his early days as a quant at JPMorgan before returning home to St. Louis to work at NISA. They also discuss the risks and benefits of the private credit market, along with the dangers of private credit going into pension funds and 401Ks. They also discuss liability investment strategies for managing over $483 billion in client assets.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Nvidia Plunges as SEC Probe Deepens AI Market Selloff | Closing Bell
items.content: <article>Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Fear and ‘Hot Sauce’: Young Investors Want To Catch Up
items.content: <article>Buzzy stocks, leveraged ETFs, and a generation feeling left behind. BlackRock’s Gargi Chaudhuri discusses ways investors can dabble in risky products while also leaning into time-proven strategies. On this week’s “Bloomberg Money”, she joins Tom Keene and Scarlet Fu, who gives a shoutout to @Eric Balchunas and his coverage of ‘hot sauce’ investment products. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Fiber Network Operator Zayo Delays Public ABS Sale Until 2027
items.author: Menghan Xiao and Reshmi Basu
items.content: <article>Fiber-optic network operator Zayo Group Holdings Inc. is delaying the public-market leg of a planned asset-backed securities offering, while moving ahead with the privately placed portion, according to people with knowledge of the matter.</article>

items.title: CrowdStrike Said in Talks to Buy Cybersecurity Firm Zscaler
items.content: <article>CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. is in talks to acquire Zscaler Inc., according to people familiar with the matter, in a deal that would be among the largest-ever in the cybersecurity sector. Zscaler, which had a market value of $32 billion at the end of regular trading Friday, rose about 16% after the close. The two companies are discussing a potential combination that could come together soon, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is confidential. Bloomberg News Deals Reporter Ryan Gould reports on the deal.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Anthropic Slides 8.5% to Shrink IPO Gain as AI Trade Unravels
items.author: Carmen Reinicke, Julien Ponthus and Neil Campling
items.content: <article>Anthropic PBC shares erased a portion of their first-day jump on Friday, testing investors’ faith after the AI lab delivered the biggest initial public offering in history.</article>

items.title: China Offshore Tax Clampdown Pushes Budget Into Rare Surplus
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China’s budget swung into a rare surplus in October, as tighter scrutiny of offshore wealth produced a one-off bonanza of individual income tax receipts and offset a long-awaited increase in fiscal spending.</article>

items.title: Billionaire Raises $720 Million Private Credit for Megha Buyout
items.author: Dipika Lalwani
items.content: <article>Indian billionaire P.V. Krishna Reddy has secured about 67 billion rupees ($720 million) from global private credit investors to buy out his uncle’s stake in Megha Engineering & Infrastructures Ltd., according to people familiar with the matter, in a layered transaction that is one of the country’s biggest deals this year.</article>

items.title: Gold Logs Worst Week Since March on Hawkish Fed, AI Selloff
items.author: Yihui Xie and Jack Ryan
items.content: <article>Gold slid for a fifth day — notching its biggest weekly decline since March — as a hawkish Federal Reserve signaled more interest-rate hikes and a rout in AI stocks spurred selling across metals markets.</article>

items.title: Nasdaq 100 Has Worst Week Since 2020 on AI Drama: Markets Wrap
items.author: Rita Nazareth
items.content: <article>Weeks of anxiety around the viability of the artificial-intelligence trade erupted into a full-blown selloff, pushing the S&P 500 to a technical correction while lifting bonds and haven currencies.</article>
